subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw accept new core lifecycle semantics for sub-agent startup progress and typed startup failure, or should this remain a diagnostic/watchdog-only problem without new phases?
rationale: The source-reproducible symptom is real, but the proposed fix changes a core lifecycle/API surface that must stay consistent across gateway, SDK, session state, and subagent consumers.

options.title: Accept a refreshed lifecycle contract
options.body: Refresh or replace the stale PR against current main, keeping the new phases additive and proving gateway, SDK, and subagent consumers handle them consistently.

options.title: Narrow to startup-failed only
options.body: Approve only a typed startup terminal failure signal and leave first-progress to existing tool/text events or later UX work.

options.title: Reject new phases
options.body: Keep the current lifecycle contract and solve this through diagnostics, watchdogs, or docs without adding new core event semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept a refreshed lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the stale PR against current main, keeping the new phases additive and proving gateway, SDK, and subagent consumers handle them consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: The history pass shows relevant subagent lifecycle and terminal outcome ownership, and this decision is primarily about the durable lifecycle contract shape.
